works/luther-magnificat/summary: Luther's commentary on Mary's song (Luke 1:46–55), written around the Diet of Worms, praising Mary's humility and God's regard for the lowly.
works/luther-magnificat/significance: Shows Luther's deep respect for Mary as a model of faith alongside his rejection of invoking her merits.
works/ineffabilis-deus/summary: Apostolic constitution of 8 December 1854 defining the Immaculate Conception of Mary.
works/ineffabilis-deus/significance: First solemn papal definition of a dogma without a council; precursor to Vatican I.
works/munificentissimus-deus/summary: Apostolic constitution of 1 November 1950 defining that Mary, having completed the course of her earthly life, was assumed body and soul into heavenly glory.
works/munificentissimus-deus/significanc: The only ex cathedra definition since Vatican I.
works/carey-enquiry/title: An Enquiry into the Obligations of Christians to Use Means for the Conversion of the Heathens
works/carey-enquiry/summary: Carey argues that the Great Commission still binds the church, surveys the world’s population and religions, and proposes a missionary society.
works/carey-enquiry/significance: Manifesto of the modern Protestant missionary movement.
works/ricci-true-meaning/title: The True Meaning of the Lord of Heaven (Tianzhu Shiyi)
works/ricci-true-meaning/summary: Dialogue between a Western and a Chinese scholar arguing from reason and the Confucian classics for the Lord of Heaven, the soul and moral cultivation.
works/ricci-true-meaning/significance: Classic of Jesuit accommodation, read by Chinese, Korean and Japanese literati.
works/kraemer-christian-message-work/tit: The Christian Message in a Non-Christian World
works/kraemer-christian-message-work/sum: Preparatory volume for the Tambaram conference on the relation of the gospel to the religions.
works/kraemer-christian-message-work/sig: Classic statement of discontinuity between revelation and religion.
works/hick-god-universe-faiths-work/titl: God and the Universe of Faiths
works/hick-god-universe-faiths-work/summ: Essays proposing a "Copernican revolution" placing God, not Christianity, at the centre of the universe of faiths.
works/hick-god-universe-faiths-work/sign: Founding text of Christian religious pluralism.
works/dignitatis-humanae/summary: Declaration on the right of persons and communities to social and civil freedom in religious matters.
works/dignitatis-humanae/significance: Marked the Catholic Church’s embrace of religious liberty.
works/dominus-iesus/summary: Declaration of the Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith on the unique and universal saving role of Christ and the Church.
works/dominus-iesus/significance: Major Catholic response to religious pluralism.
works/sanneh-translating-message-work/ti: Translating the Message: The Missionary Impact on Culture
works/sanneh-translating-message-work/su: Historical study of Bible translation and vernacular renewal from the early church to modern Africa.
works/sanneh-translating-message-work/si: Reframed the debate on mission and colonialism.
works/campbell-declaration-and-address/t: Declaration and Address of the Christian Association of Washington
works/campbell-declaration-and-address/s: Thomas Campbell’s manifesto calling Christians to unite on the basis of the Bible alone, without creeds as terms of communion.
Charter document of the Stone-Campbell Restoration Movement.
works/book-of-mormon/summary: Published by Joseph Smith in Palmyra, New York, as a translation of ancient American records; regarded by Latter-day Saints as scripture alongside the Bible.
works/book-of-mormon/significance: Foundational scripture of the Latter-day Saint movement; not accepted as scripture by any Nicene church.
works/wentworth-letter/title: The Wentworth Letter (including the Articles of Faith)
works/wentworth-letter/summary: Joseph Smith’s account of the church’s origins for a Chicago editor, published in Times and Seasons (1 March 1842), ending with thirteen "Articles of Faith".
works/wentworth-letter/significance: The Articles of Faith became a canonised summary of Latter-day Saint belief (Pearl of Great Price).
works/russell-divine-plan-of-the-ages/ti: The Divine Plan of the Ages (Millennial Dawn / Studies in the Scriptures, vol. 1)
works/russell-divine-plan-of-the-ages/su: First volume of Charles Taze Russell’s series setting out the Bible Students’ chronology and theology.
works/russell-divine-plan-of-the-ages/si: Foundational for the Bible Student movement and Jehovah’s Witnesses.
works/harnack-what-is-christianity/title: What Is Christianity? (Das Wesen des Christentums)
works/harnack-what-is-christianity/summa: Sixteen public lectures given in Berlin in the winter of 1899–1900.
works/harnack-what-is-christianity/signi: Classic popular statement of liberal Protestantism; English translation by T. B. Saunders (1901).
works/pascendi-dominici-gregis/summary: Encyclical of Pius X on the doctrines of the Modernists.
works/pascendi-dominici-gregis/significa: Condemned Catholic Modernism as "the synthesis of all heresies"; followed by the Anti-Modernist Oath (1910–1967).
works/mott-evangelization-of-the-world/t: The Evangelization of the World in This Generation
works/mott-evangelization-of-the-world/s: John R. Mott’s exposition of the Student Volunteer Movement’s watchword.
Expressed the confidence of the missionary movement on the eve of Edinburgh 1910.
works/the-fundamentals/title: The Fundamentals: A Testimony to the Truth
works/the-fundamentals/summary: Ninety essays in twelve volumes (1910–15), funded by oilmen Lyman and Milton Stewart and edited by A. C. Dixon, Louis Meyer and R. A. Torrey, defending inerrancy, the virgin birth, the atonement, the resurrection and miracles, and criticising higher criticism, evolutionism, Romanism and new religions.
works/the-fundamentals/significance: About three million copies were distributed free to pastors, missionaries and students; gave "fundamentalism" its name.
works/machen-christianity-and-liberalism: Machen’s argument that liberalism and historic Christianity are two different religions, compared doctrine by doctrine.
The most intellectually serious fundamentalist-era critique of liberalism; admired even by some secular critics such as Walter Lippmann.
works/fosdick-shall-the-fundamentalists-: Sermon preached at First Presbyterian Church, New York, 21 May 1922, and widely circulated in print.
Triggered the Presbyterian phase of the Fundamentalist–Modernist controversy.
works/barth-epistle-to-the-romans/title: The Epistle to the Romans (Der Römerbrief)
works/barth-epistle-to-the-romans/summar: Karl Barth’s commentary on Romans (1919; radically rewritten 1922), stressing God’s otherness and judgement on all religion.
works/barth-epistle-to-the-romans/signif: Inaugurated "dialectical theology" or neo-orthodoxy; described as a bomb dropped on the theologians’ playground (Karl Adam).
works/unitatis-redintegratio/summary: Vatican II’s decree on ecumenism, promulgated by Paul VI on 21 November 1964.
works/unitatis-redintegratio/significanc: Committed the Catholic Church to the ecumenical movement and recognised other Christians as brothers and sisters in the Lord.
works/lausanne-covenant/summary: Statement of the International Congress on World Evangelization (Lausanne, July 1974), drafted by a committee chaired by John Stott.
works/lausanne-covenant/significance: Defining statement of global evangelicalism, affirming evangelism and social responsibility.
works/nee-normal-christian-church-life/s: Watchman Nee’s lectures on church order (originally in Chinese as Rethinking Our Work, 1938), teaching one church per locality led by local elders.
Shaped the Local Church movement and Chinese indigenous and house-church ecclesiology.
works/walls-missionary-movement-work/tit: The Missionary Movement in Christian History
works/walls-missionary-movement-work/sum: Collected essays by Andrew Walls on the transmission of the Christian faith across cultures.
works/walls-missionary-movement-work/sig: Influential framing of the southward shift of world Christianity.
works/bell-love-wins/summary: Rob Bell’s book questioning traditional teaching on hell and suggesting hope for universal reconciliation.
works/bell-love-wins/significance: A flashpoint in debates over progressive evangelicalism.
works/evans-searching-for-sunday/title: Searching for Sunday: Loving, Leaving, and Finding the Church
works/evans-searching-for-sunday/summary: Rachel Held Evans’ memoir of leaving evangelicalism and finding a home in the Episcopal Church, structured around the seven sacraments.
works/justin-second-apology/summary: Short appeal to the Roman Senate after the execution of Christians, arguing that the Logos sowed “seeds” of truth among the philosophers.
works/justin-second-apology/significance: Classic source of the “seeds of the Word” (logos spermatikos) tradition of positive engagement with philosophy.
works/john-damascus-on-heresies/summary: A catalogue of heresies ending with the “heresy of the Ishmaelites”, an early Christian account and critique of Islam written under Umayyad rule.
works/john-damascus-on-heresies/signific: The earliest substantial Christian treatment of Islam, setting the tone of Byzantine polemic.
works/timothy-dialogue-al-mahdi/summary: Record, in Syriac (later Arabic), of a two-day courteous debate between Catholicos Timothy I and the Abbasid caliph on the Trinity, incarnation, Scripture and Muhammad.
works/timothy-dialogue-al-mahdi/signific: A model of respectful Christian–Muslim theological dialogue, widely copied in the Christian East.
works/anselm-proslogion/summary: A prayerful meditation proposing that God is “that than which nothing greater can be thought” and that such a being must exist in reality.
works/anselm-proslogion/significance: Origin of the ontological argument and of the motto “faith seeking understanding”.
works/pascal-pensees/summary: Fragments of an unfinished apology for Christianity, published posthumously, including the “wager” and reflections on the heart, human greatness and misery.
works/pascal-pensees/significance: A classic of existential and pragmatic apologetics.
works/butler-analogy/title: The Analogy of Religion, Natural and Revealed
works/butler-analogy/summary: Answers deism by arguing that revealed religion has no greater difficulties than the natural order deists accept, and that probability is the guide of life.
works/butler-analogy/significance: The most influential English apologetic of the 18th century and a model of evidential, probabilistic reasoning.
works/hume-dialogues/summary: Posthumous dialogue in which Philo dismantles the design argument proposed by Cleanthes.
works/hume-dialogues/significance: Classic philosophical critique of natural theology.
works/paley-natural-theology/title: Natural Theology; or, Evidences of the Existence and Attributes of the Deity
works/paley-natural-theology/summary: Argues from the contrivance and adaptation of living things — compared to a watch — to an intelligent and benevolent designer.
works/paley-natural-theology/significanc: The classic statement of the design argument, later undercut for many by Darwin.
works/pfander-mizan-al-haqq/summary: Argues that the Bible has not been corrupted, that Christianity fulfils the criteria of true revelation and that Islam does not.
works/pfander-mizan-al-haqq/significance: The most influential missionary apologetic to Muslims in the 19th century; still reprinted.
works/kierkegaard-postscript/title: Concluding Unscientific Postscript to Philosophical Fragments
works/kierkegaard-postscript/summary: Under the pseudonym Johannes Climacus, argues that subjectivity is truth and that faith is a passionate appropriation of an objective uncertainty, not a result of historical or speculative proof.
works/kierkegaard-postscript/significanc: Foundational text of Christian existentialism and modern fideism.
works/dei-filius/title: Dei Filius (Dogmatic Constitution on the Catholic Faith)
works/dei-filius/summary: First Vatican Council’s constitution on God, revelation, faith and reason: God can be known with certainty by natural reason from created things; revelation is nonetheless morally necessary and faith is reasonable.
works/dei-filius/significance: Defined Catholic teaching on natural theology against both rationalism and fideism.
works/brunner-nature-and-grace/summary: Argues for a formal (but not material) image of God surviving the fall, a “point of contact” for the gospel and a limited revelation in creation.
works/brunner-nature-and-grace/significa: Provoked Barth’s No!, the most famous intra-Protestant debate on natural theology.
works/barth-nein/title: No! An Answer to Emil Brunner (Nein! Antwort an Emil Brunner)
works/barth-nein/summary: Rejects any natural theology or point of contact independent of God’s revelation in Jesus Christ.
works/barth-nein/significance: Written months after the Barmen Declaration; a manifesto of revelation-centred theology.
works/lewis-mere-christianity/summary: Edited from BBC radio talks (1941-44): the moral argument, the core of Christian belief and ethics, and the “trilemma” about Jesus’ identity.
works/lewis-mere-christianity/significan: The most widely read popular apologetic of the 20th century.
works/van-til-defense-of-faith/summary: Sets out presuppositional apologetics and criticises classical and evidential methods as granting the unbeliever’s autonomy.
works/plantinga-warranted-christian-beli: Argues that if Christianity is true, Christian belief is likely warranted through the sensus divinitatis and the internal testimony of the Holy Spirit, without needing evidential arguments.
